cautions: This subject is health-adjacent. Lessons must never give individualized clinical, diagnostic, treatment, legal, or benefits-eligibility advice. Teach practice concepts, not case direction.
Crisis content must be handled carefully: describe professional practice, name 988 as the current U.S. crisis line, and avoid anything resembling instructions for self-management of a crisis.

The NASW Code of Ethics is copyrighted. Cite and describe its standards in original wording; never reproduce its text. State that codes vary by profession and jurisdiction and that licensure law governs.

Motivational interviewing has a defined evidence base and defined limits; attribute to Miller and Rollnick, use current (fourth edition) framing, and do not present it as a technique for making people comply.

ACEs research is widely oversimplified: the original study population was largely white, insured, and middle-class, and ACE scores were never designed as an individual screening or predictive tool. Say so.
Poverty figures are time-sensitive; date every statistic and distinguish the Official Poverty Measure, the Supplemental Poverty Measure, and the HHS poverty guidelines.
Cultural humility (Tervalon & Murray-García 1998) is a distinct concept from cultural competence — attribute it correctly and do not merge them.
